question_text: The speed of a cricket player's bowl is recorded as $141.6\text{ km h}^{-1}$, rounded to 1 decimal place. In what range of values does the actual speed $s$ lie?

subparts.stem: The speed of a cricket player's bowl is recorded as $141.6\text{ km h}^{-1}$, rounded to 1 decimal place. In what range of values does the actual speed $s$ lie?

mark_breakdown.desc: Calculating the absolute error limit as half the smallest scale unit
Correct lower and upper bounds of speed

subparts.solution:
The measuring device is accurate to $\pm \frac{0.1}{2}\text{ km\,h}^{-1} = \pm 0.05\text{ km\,h}^{-1}$.
$\therefore$ the range of values is $141.6 \pm 0.05\text{ km\,h}^{-1}$.
The cricket player's actual bowling speed lies between $141.55\text{ km\,h}^{-1}$ and $141.65\text{ km\,h}^{-1}$.
$\therefore 141.55\text{ km\,h}^{-1} < s < 141.65\text{ km\,h}^{-1}$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: The maximum error of a measurement is half of the precision/smallest unit of measurement: $\text{limit of reading} = \frac{1}{2} \times \text{unit}$.
step_by_step: The speed is given to 1 decimal place ($0.1$), so error is $\pm \frac{0.1}{2} = \pm 0.05\text{ km\,h}^{-1}$.
State the inequality: $141.55\text{ km\,h}^{-1} < s < 141.65\text{ km\,h}^{-1}$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Using $\pm 0.1$ instead of dividing the measurement unit by 2.
